issue.title: False positive `unbalanced-tuple-unpacking` when unpacking an exception's `args`
issue.body:
### Bug description

astroid models `BaseException.args` on an exception instance as a *known empty* tuple (`ExceptionInstanceModel.attr_args` returns `nodes.Tuple()` with no elements). Pylint's `unbalanced-tuple-unpacking` therefore reports "right side has 0 values" whenever code unpacks `exc.args`, even though the length of `args` is simply unknown.

The stdlib does this in `importlib/metadata/__init__.py`:

```python
class PackageNotFoundError(ModuleNotFoundError):
    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        (name,) = self.args
        return name
```

Minimal example:

```python
def f():
    try:
        pass
    except ValueError as exc:
        (message,) = exc.args
        first, second = exc.args
        return message, first, second
    return None
```

### Configuration

_No response_

### Command used

```shell
pylint --disable=all --enable=unbalanced-tuple-unpacking a.py
```

### Pylint output

```shell
************* Module a
a.py:5:8: W0632: Possible unbalanced tuple unpacking with sequence : left side has 1 label, right side has 0 values (unbalanced-tuple-unpacking)
a.py:6:8: W0632: Possible unbalanced tuple unpacking with sequence : left side has 2 labels, right side has 0 values (unbalanced-tuple-unpacking)
```

### Expected behavior

No message. The contents of `args` are not known from the instance alone, so the check cannot say the unpacking is unbalanced.

### Pylint version

```shell
pylint 4.1.0-dev0
astroid 4.4.0-dev0
Python 3.13.11
```

### OS / Environment

macOS

### Additional dependencies

_No response_

```python
                                                 ^^^^^^^^^
```


(Intermediate `_infer_stmts`/`infer` frames elided.)

The defect is in `starred_assigned_stmts` in `astroid/protocols.py`. For a starred name nested in a `for` target, it walks a chain of index lookups into each element of the iterable, ending with a slice lookup that extracts the starred elements as a list. Whatever iterates `elts` next crashes.

The same happens with a plain name in that position:

```python

for a, (b, *c) in [[1, x]]:
    c  # TypeError: 'Name' object is not iterable
```

and through the `IndexError` path when the inner sequence is too short:

```python

    c  # TypeError: 'List' object is not iterable
```

issue.title: PyO3 complex enums cause linting to hang
issue.body:
Compiling the below Rust code gives me a working binary, that I can then import as a module and run without any issues. However when I try to run pylint on the code that calls it pylint simply just hangs while trying to lint the binary.

_This issue was originally reported here: https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint/issues/10513_

```rust
use pyo3::types::PyModuleMethods;

#[pyo3::pyclass]
#[pyo3(module = "happy_hour.refreshments")]
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum Cocktails {
    Mojito {
        sugar: u32,
        rum: u32,
        mint: u32,
        lime_wedges: u32,
        soda_water: u32,
        consumers: Vec<u32>,
    },
    MintJulep {
        bourbon: u32,
        mint: u32,
        consumers: Vec<u32>,
    },
}

#[pyo3::pymodule]
fn refreshments(
    py: pyo3::Python<'_>,
    m: &pyo3::Bound<pyo3::prelude::PyModule>,
) -> pyo3::PyResult<()> {
    m.add_class::<Cocktails>()?;

    return Ok(());
}
```

This essentially boils down to this:

```python
class Cocktails:
    @final
    class Mojito(Cocktails):
        sugar: int
        rum: int
        mint: int
        lime_wedges: int
        soda_water: int
        consumers: list[int]

    @final
    class MintJulep(Cocktails):
        bourbon: int
        mint: int
        consumers: list[int]
```

When I build and try to lint this example: [PYLINT-10513.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32197827/PYLINT-10513.zip) pylint hangs.
Pausing a debugger we can tell that the parsing gets stuck at this loop: https://github.com/pylint-dev/astroid/blob/b5051ff170e8fbe46ff217d21c837898a4209c04/astroid/nodes/node_ng.py#L321

_Please note, the original issue was using older versions of pylint and astroid. I've used pylint 4.0.8 and astroid 4.0.4 to re-test this. The above reflects this._


In addition to this @Pierre-Sassoulas managed to [reproduce](https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint/issues/10513#issuecomment-5652913317) it in pure Python:

> A pyo3 complex enum attaches each variant to the enum class, so every variant also sees its siblings through inheritance. Recreating just that shape with live Python classes hangs the exact same way:
> 
> ```python
> """Pure-Python stand-in for the pyo3 complex enum of issue 10513."""
> import sys
> import types
> 
> import astroid
> 
> fruit_basket = types.ModuleType("fruit_basket")
> 
> 
> class Fruit:
>     """Stands in for the pyo3 enum itself."""
> 
> 
> class Apple(Fruit):
>     """Stands in for a variant of the enum."""
> 
> 
> class Banana(Fruit):
>     """Stands in for another variant of the enum."""
> 
> 
> # pyo3 attaches each variant to the enum class, so every variant sees its
> # siblings through inheritance.
> Fruit.Apple = Apple
> Fruit.Banana = Banana
> for klass in (Fruit, Apple, Banana):
>     klass.__module__ = "fruit_basket"
>     setattr(fruit_basket, klass.__name__, klass)
> sys.modules["fruit_basket"] = fruit_basket
> 
> print("building...", flush=True)
> astroid.MANAGER.ast_from_module(fruit_basket, "fruit_basket")
> print("built fine")
> ```
> 
> It prints `building...` and never returns.
> 
> ### What happens
> 
> It is not infinite recursion — `InspectBuilder._done` bounds that, and fewer than 200 `object_build()` calls happen before it gets stuck. It is an infinite *loop* over a cyclic parent chain.
> 
> `ScopedNode._append_node()` ends with `child.parent = self` (`astroid/nodes/scoped_nodes/mixin.py:121`), so `InspectBuilder.object_build()` **re-parents a node it has already built** when the same live class turns up again under a different owner. With mutually visible siblings that produces `Apple.parent = Banana` *and* `Banana.parent = Apple`. Detecting the cycle while building your zip gives:
> 
> ```
> PARENT CYCLE: ClassDef:Cocktails_Mojito -> ClassDef:Cocktails_MintJulep
> ```
> 
> `NodeNG.root()` then spins forever in its `while parent.parent:` walk (`astroid/nodes/node_ng.py:322`). Every stack sample lands in the same place:
> 
> ```
>   File "astroid/nodes/node_ng.py", line 322 in root
>   File "astroid/interpreter/objectmodel.py", line 558 in attr___module__
>   File "astroid/nodes/scoped_nodes/scoped_nodes.py", line 1935 in implicit_locals
>   File "astroid/nodes/scoped_nodes/scoped_nodes.py", line 1919 in __init__
>   File "astroid/raw_building.py", line 111 in build_class
>   File "astroid/raw_building.py", line 371 in _base_class_object_build
>   File "astroid/raw_building.py", line 275 in object_build_class
>   File "astroid/raw_building.py", line 514 in object_build
> ```

issue.title: Crash in infer_typing_alias on non-int _alias() second argument
issue.body:
### Steps to reproduce

```python
import astroid

node = astroid.extract_node('''
from typing import _alias
x = _alias(int, "foo")
''')
node.value.inferred()
```

### Current behavior

Inference raises an uncaught `TypeError`:

```
  File ".../astroid/brain/brain_typing.py", line 332, in infer_typing_alias
    if isinstance(maybe_type_var, nodes.Const) and maybe_type_var.value > 0:
TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'
```

`infer_typing_alias` decides whether the aliased class is subscriptable by comparing the
second argument's constant value with `0`, but only checks that the argument is a
`Const` first. The `_looks_like_typing_alias` predicate matches any two-argument call to
a function named `_alias`/`_DeprecatedGenericAlias` whose first argument is a name or
attribute, so a `str`, `bytes` or `None` second argument reaches the comparison and
crashes. `None` and `b"x"` fail the same way.

### Expected behavior

Inference returns a result (the non-subscriptable `ClassDef`) instead of crashing, the
same as it already does for a legitimate non-positive count like `_alias(tuple, -1)`.

### `python -c "from astroid import __pkginfo__; print(__pkginfo__.version)"` output

4.4.0-dev0 (main, confirmed on current `main`)

The brain still keeps the original (invalid) names in `instance_attrs` instead of substituting `_1`, `_2`, … for each duplicate or keyword-named field. Two synthetic cases:

```python
import astroid

# Case 1: 'def' is a Python keyword -> at runtime it becomes _1
node = astroid.extract_node('''
from collections import namedtuple
Tag = namedtuple("Tag", ["id", "def", "a"], rename=True)
Tag(1, 2, 3)  #@
''')
```

issue.title: Source file remains open after a decoding error
issue.body:
### Steps to reproduce

Run this on current main. The wrapper records real file objects so their closed state remains observable after the read fails:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from unittest.mock import patch

from astroid.builder import AstroidBuilder
from astroid.exceptions import AstroidBuildingError
from astroid.manager import AstroidManager

builder = AstroidBuilder(AstroidManager())
streams = []

def tracked_open(*args, **kwargs):
    stream = open(*args, **kwargs)
    streams.append(stream)
    return stream

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    source = Path(directory) / "invalid_encoding.py"
    source.write_bytes(b"# coding: utf-8\n\nvalue = '\xff'\n")
    try:
        with patch("astroid.builder.open", side_effect=tracked_open):
            try:
                builder.file_build(str(source), "invalid_encoding")
            except AstroidBuildingError as error:
                print(type(error.__cause__).__name__)
                print([stream.closed for stream in streams])
    finally:
        for stream in streams:
            stream.close()
```

```text
UnicodeDecodeError
[True, False]
```

The binary stream used to detect the encoding is closed, but the text stream stays open while the decoding exception is retained. `open_source_file()` raises before `file_build()` reaches its `with stream` block.

### Expected behavior

Close the text stream when reading fails, while preserving the existing `AstroidBuildingError` and its cause.
